request.spec:
A button downloads the people of the whole tree as a CSV file: a header line
sheet,name,grade,due-total then one line per person, this sheet first in list order, then the
other sheets of the tree by sheet id.
request.prompt:

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A button downloads the people of the whole tree as a CSV file: a header line

agent.result_text:
I added an "Export tree (CSV)" button, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

The button (`data-testid="export-tree"`) downloads a file whose first line is `sheet,name,grade,due-total`. Then comes one line per person: this sheet's people first in list order, then the rest of the tree by sheet id. Retired people are included. A person with no due-total shows `n/a`, as the test expects. For example, exporting from the child sheet lists its own people first, then the parent's.

All of the change is in `src/main/frontend/features/export/export.slot.tsx`; the server and stored data didn't need changing. The app already had an endpoint, `/api/sheets/{id}/tree`, that returns the other sheets of a tree (the tree search uses it). The new button copies that search's approach:

- On each press it fetches the tree and drops the cached data for the other sheets, so they are re-read from the store and show what another user changed.
- It works out each sheet's due-totals with the same code the sheet's own screen uses, then downloads the file once every sheet has reported.

The current sheet's data isn't re-fetched when you press the button; it's taken from what's already on screen. The tree search works the same way.
